statement: Let F_1 be the permutations of S_4 with exactly one fixed point and use Pan's left-Cayley convention. Then F_1 is the set of eight 3-cycles and equals A_4 minus V_4, where V_4={1,(12)(34),(13)(24),(14)(23)}. The graph Cay(S_4,F_1) is isomorphic to A(4,4,3) and to the disjoint union 2K_{4,4,4}; its two components are the parity classes and the three parts in each component are the left V_4-cosets. Its full graph automorphism group is (S_4 wr S_3) wr S_2, of order 13,759,414,272. Pan's Conjecture 3.1 in arXiv:2407.19745v1 prescribes a group of order 1,152 at (n,t)=(4,1), so that conjecture is disproved at this parameter.
contribution: A complete elementary resolution of the frozen first intervening parameter: it classifies the graph and every graph automorphism, rather than only exhibiting an unexpected automorphism. The claim is scoped to the conjecture as stated in the frozen arXiv v1; the inaccessible journal full text and priority remain explicitly unclaimed.
